# Judith Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Holofernes looked at her and said, "Courage, woman. Don't be afraid. I have never hurt anyone who chose to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of all the earth.

**2** If your people in the hill country hadn't insulted me, I would never have raised a spear against them. They brought this on themselves.

**3** So tell me — why did you leave them and come to us? You came to the right place. You're safe now. Tonight and every night after this.

**4** No one will lay a hand on you. You will be treated as well as any servant of my lord King Nebuchadnezzar deserves."

**5** Judith answered him, "Listen to what I have to say. Let your handmaid speak freely before you — I will tell you nothing false tonight, my lord.

**6** Follow what I tell you, and through your hands God himself will bring his purpose to completion. My lord will not fail in anything he intends.

**7** I swear by the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of all the earth, and by the life of his power — he who sent you to restore order among all living creatures — not only do human beings serve him through you, but the animals of the field, the herds, and the birds in the sky will all live by your strength, under Nebuchadnezzar and all his house.

**8** We have all heard of your wisdom, your mind's extraordinary cunning. It is spoken of to the ends of the earth: you alone are worthy in all the kingdom, formidable in knowledge, breathtaking in military genius.

**9** Now — about what Achior said in your council. We heard about it. The men of Bethulia rescued him and he told them everything he had said before you.

**10** Don't set his words aside, my master and lord. Hold them close, because they are true. Our people cannot be punished, the sword cannot touch them — unless they sin against their God.

**11** And now, so that my lord need not march home empty-handed and defeated, death itself has come down on them. Sin has seized them by the throat. They are about to do what will drive their God to fury.

**12** Their food ran out. Their water is nearly gone. They made a decision: they would slaughter their livestock. Then they decided to go further — to eat the very things God's own law forbids.

**13** The firstfruits of the grain, the tithes of wine and oil — the offerings they had already consecrated and set aside for the priests who serve before our God's face in Jerusalem. Things no ordinary Israelite may even touch —

**14** they have voted to eat them. And they have sent people to Jerusalem — where others have already done the same — to get the council of elders to authorize it.

**15** The moment that authorization arrives and they act on it, they will be delivered into destruction that very day.

**16** That is why I, your servant, knowing all this, fled from them. God himself sent me to you, to do things with you that will leave the whole earth stunned — everyone who hears of it.

**17** I am a woman who fears God. I serve the God of heaven day and night. I will stay with you, my lord. Every night I will go out to the valley and pray to God, and he will tell me when they have committed their offense.

**18** Then I will come and tell you. You will march out with your full army, and not a single one of them will be able to stand against you.

**19** I will lead you straight through Judea until we reach Jerusalem. I will set your throne in the very heart of the city. You will drive them like sheep without a shepherd — not a dog will so much as growl in your direction. All of this was shown to me ahead of time. It was told to me. I was sent to bring this word to you."

**20** Her words delighted Holofernes. They delighted all his servants. They stared at her in wonder.

**21** "There is no woman like her," they said, "anywhere on the face of the earth — not for beauty, not for wisdom."

**22** Holofernes said to her, "God did well to send you out ahead of your people — so that the power will be ours, and those who defied my lord will be destroyed.

**23** You are beautiful to look at, and your words are beautiful too. If you do what you've promised, your God shall be my God, and you will live in the palace of King Nebuchadnezzar — and your fame will spread over all the earth."

---
*PNEUMA notes: Judith is performing here — flattery layered over double-truth. Every oath she swears is technically true but means something entirely different than Holofernes hears. The irony is at full pitch throughout. "Sin has seized them by the throat" is an interpretive expansion of v. 11's "sin has seized them."*
